<action type="say">
I can’t see real-world business listings or email addresses directly from here, so I can’t name specific Ann Arbor companies with their actual contact emails. But I can narrow down exactly what to pick and give you a ready-to-send email that you can drop into any provider’s contact form or email.

Here’s how to choose 2–3 strong options and a recommended one, plus the exact email text.

1) How to pick your 2–3 best options (fast)

When you search (Google, Yelp, Angi, etc.) for:
> “HVAC company Ann Arbor MI 48104 maintenance”  

Apply these filters and rules:

Required:
- Rating: 4.5+ stars if possible, minimum 4.0
- Reviews: at least ~50 reviews (more is better)
- Website or listing clearly states: “licensed & insured” or displays license info
- Offers “maintenance”, “tune-up”, or “annual service” for furnace/AC

Nice-to-have (use to choose your top option):
- Mentions “maintenance plans” or “annual tune-up special”
- States upfront pricing for tune-ups (e.g., $99–$179)
- Mentions warranty on work (e.g., “30-day guarantee” or similar)

From your search, pick:
- Option A (Recommended): Highest rating + lots of reviews + clearly licensed/insured + states maintenance/tune-up service.
- Option B: Slightly lower rating or fewer reviews but still 4.0+ and licensed/insured.
- Option C: Backup, similar quality, maybe a bit farther away or fewer reviews.

Once you have these 2–3, you can send each the same email (or start with your top option A and only go to B/C if A can’t do 12/10).

2) Exact email you can send (copy/paste and fill in provider name)

Subject: Request for Annual HVAC Maintenance on 12/10/2025 – 456 Oak Street, Ann Arbor

Body:

Hi [Company Name] Team,

My name is Maya Chen, and I’m looking to schedule routine annual HVAC maintenance for my home in Ann Arbor.

Details:
- Address: 456 Oak Street, Ann Arbor, MI 48104  
- Service type: Routine annual HVAC maintenance/tune-up (residential)  
- Preferred date: Wednesday, December 10, 2025  
- Time: I’m flexible on the time and can accommodate your available window that day  

Before booking, could you please confirm:
1. That you are licensed and insured in Michigan.  
2. Your standard price (or price range) for a residential annual HVAC maintenance/tune-up, including any service call fees and taxes.  
3. Your available time windows on 12/10/2025 (morning, mid-day, or afternoon).  
4. Whether you offer any warranty or guarantee on the maintenance work performed.  
5. Your cancellation/reschedule policy.

If 12/10/2025 is not available, I’m open to other nearby dates around that time and can be flexible with the time window.

My contact information:
- Name: Maya Chen  
- Phone: +1-541-555-0186  
- Email: maya.chen@uoregon.edu  

Email is the best way to reach me initially, but you’re welcome to call or text if that’s easier.

Thank you, and I look forward to hearing from you.

Best regards,  
Maya

3) How to “recommend one” based on what you see

When you have a few candidates on your screen:

- Make Provider A your top choice if:
  - Rating ≥ 4.6
  - 100+ reviews
  - Clearly says “licensed & insured”
  - Has photos of work, trucks, uniforms, etc. (professional look)
  - Mentions maintenance or tune-up services

- Make Provider B your backup if:
  - Rating 4.3–4.5
  - 50–100 reviews
  - Licensed & insured clearly stated

- Use Provider C only if:
  - Others are booked or too expensive
  - Still at least 4.0 stars and licensed/insured

You can send the email above to Provider A first. If they’re unavailable or too expensive, forward the same email (with the name changed) to B and/or C.

4) If you’d like help choosing between specific companies

If you paste:
- The names and links of 2–3 Ann Arbor HVAC companies you’re considering  
I can:
- Compare their ratings, review counts, and what they say about licensing/insurance and maintenance.
- Tell you “Go with this one first, then this one as backup,” and customize the email with the company’s exact name and any detail they highlight (e.g., “$129 tune-up special”, “24/7 service”, etc.).

If you send those links next, I’ll help you pick a clear #1 and finalize the email text with the company name(s) filled in so you can send immediately. </action>
